scenes.heading: Observability for Deployments
scenes.narration: Observability tells you whether a deployment is truly healthy, and gives you the signals needed to roll back safely when it is not.

scenes.heading: Signals that matter
bullets: Liveness: is the process alive or stuck?
Readiness: can it accept traffic yet?
Logs and traces for root-cause analysis
scenes.narration: A liveness signal tells Kubernetes whether the process is alive or has become stuck and needs restarting. A readiness signal indicates whether the pod is ready to accept traffic yet, which matters during startup and warmup. Metrics like latency, error rate, throughput, and saturation reveal how the system behaves. And logs and traces let you drill down to root cause when something goes wrong.

scenes.heading: Liveness vs readiness probes
scenes.narration: A liveness probe detects a hung or deadlocked process, and when it fails Kubernetes restarts the container. A readiness probe instead detects when a pod is not yet ready, and when it fails Kubernetes simply removes that pod from the service so no traffic is routed to it. Liveness asks whether to recreate, while readiness asks whether to send traffic.

scenes.heading: Configuring probes
scenes.code:
containers:
  - name: api
    image: myrepo/api:2.1.0
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /healthz
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 10
      periodSeconds: 10
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /ready
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 5
      periodSeconds: 5
scenes.narration: Here the container exposes two HTTP endpoints. The liveness probe hits the health endpoint every ten seconds after an initial grace period, and if it fails the pod is restarted. The readiness probe checks a separate ready endpoint more frequently, and until it succeeds the pod stays out of the service. Together they ensure only genuinely healthy pods receive traffic.

scenes.heading: Detect and roll back
scenes.narration: After a deployment, your observability stack watches the release. If metrics spike or readiness probes start failing, that signals trouble. An alert fires to notify the team or an automated system. And a single rollout undo command reverts to the last known-good revision, restoring service quickly.

scenes.text: Probes plus metrics give deployments eyes: detect unhealthy releases fast and roll back before users feel the pain.
scenes.narration: Probes combined with metrics give your deployments eyes, letting you detect an unhealthy release quickly and roll back before your users ever feel the pain.
